# The workflow is named, not shipped: a machine drives nothing until the
# config declares one, so this run names the one it is driving. The settings
# under it are the workflow's vocabulary — the status a ticket lands in for
# QA, and the ceilings its decisions read — because they belong to the profile
# that drives, not to the machine.
workflows:
  tickets:
    workflow: "@amykit/workflow-ticket-to-qa"
    plugins:
      - "@amykit/plugin-file-queue"
      - "@amykit/plugin-file-store"
      - "@amykit/plugin-file-brief-store"
      - "@amykit/plugin-file-notes"
      - "@amykit/plugin-github"
      - "@amykit/plugin-linear"
      - "@amykit/workflow-ticket-to-qa"
      - "@amykit/plugin-file-worktree"
      - "@amykit/plugin-claude"
      - "@amykit/plugin-codex"
      - "@amykit/plugin-agent-relay"
      - "@amykit/plugin-notify-fanout"
      - "@amykit/plugin-notify-inbox"
      - "@amykit/plugin-serial-engine"
      - "@amykit/plugin-telegram"
      - "@amykit/plugin-command-gate"
    settings:
      qaStatusName: In QA

      # Zero, because the queue is the schedule and this run is driven a move
      # at a time. In production these are the minutes a waiting state backs
      # off for.
      policy:
        maxOpenReviewsPerReviewer: 2
        pollBackoffMs: 0
        rosterBackoffMs: 0
defaultWorkflow: tickets

# Package updates have their own installed scenario. This one drives more
# than twenty single-move invocations and must not turn its twentieth move
# into a registry call unrelated to the lifecycle under proof.
autoUpdate:
  enabled: false

plugins:
  "@amykit/plugin-telegram":
    operator: "4021"
    server: http://127.0.0.1:52692
  "@amykit/plugin-file-worktree":
    repos:
      - acme/widgets
      - acme/gadgets
    workspaceRoot: /var/folders/ql/h_cgdz7j2t32wh9xdp1cwyfr0000gn/T/amy-chat-JCUToc/checkouts
    # One repository names its own root: the checkout is under a parent
    # nothing else in this config shares, which is the claim — no symlink,
    # and nothing under the root that is not state.
    checkouts:
      acme/gadgets: /var/folders/ql/h_cgdz7j2t32wh9xdp1cwyfr0000gn/T/amy-chat-JCUToc/elsewhere/gadgets
    defaultBranch: main
    root: /var/folders/ql/h_cgdz7j2t32wh9xdp1cwyfr0000gn/T/amy-chat-JCUToc/worktrees
    retentionDays: 0
  # A real gate: two shell commands, run in the checkout, and the second one
  # fails until the work is actually right. The first writes down which tree
  # it ran in and at which commit, which is what the lanes are held to.
  "@amykit/plugin-command-gate":
    gate:
      acme/widgets:
        - echo "$(pwd) $(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$AMY_E2E_WORLD/gate-heads.log"
        - test -f invoice.md
        - grep -q "currency:" invoice.md
      acme/gadgets:
        - test -f credit-note.md
        - grep -q "currency:" credit-note.md
  # The tracker's slice. A hand-written slice is merged over the derived
  # one, so only the settings somebody meant to change need to be named — and
  # the tracker's vocabulary lives nowhere but here, which is the point.
  "@amykit/plugin-slack":
    channel: C0WORK
    token: env:SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
    operator: U0OWNER
  "@amykit/plugin-linear":
    workingStatusName: In Progress
    repoByTeam:
      BILL: acme/widgets
      OPS: acme/gadgets
    defaultRepo: acme/widgets
    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:52691/graphql

agent:
  model: sonnet
  ladder: ["claude:sonnet", "claude:opus"]
  budget:
    perFiveHours: { tokens: 20000000, costUsd: 50 }
    perWeek: { tokens: 100000000, costUsd: 200 }
    stopAt: 0.9

# The question the machine asks the person, and what they answered on the
# ticket. The comment amy leaves is the first, quoted in the prompt as its own;

notify:
  hermes: null
  inbox: true
